title: Media timing and audiovisual evidence
summary: Source frame presentation timestamps (PTS) are the alignment authority. ASR word timing is an estimate relative to the extracted audio stream; mapping must preserve audio and video stream-start offsets.
invariants: Do not assign timestamps from frameIndex/24 when source PTS exists.
A02 was 24 fps at inspection, but other footage can have nonzero start times and variable frame spacing.
A word candidate must retain source video and prepared-audio hashes, clip identity, interval and transcription provider/version.
Missing word timestamps, reversed intervals and mismatched hashes fail closed.
Full facial mesh, mouth movement and speech transcription are separate evidence sources; face detection does not imply full mesh verification.
procedure: Decode bounded clips preserving frame PTS.
Acquire independent word start/end offsets from Google or Azure speech providers.
Project offsets into source-video time using source audio/video start difference.
Join word intervals to frame intervals and preserve uncertainty, quality and provenance.
Require human hearing and visual review before asset promotion.

provenance.claim: Independent timestamped transcription gateway and local face-analysis seam.
FFmpeg PTS range tracking and checkpoint interface, with MediaPipe not runtime-qualified.
